summary: Tehama is a city of 427 people packed into less than a square mile — roughly the footprint of a modest college campus — perched on the western bank of the Sacramento River in the upper Sacramento Valley, about halfway between Red Bluff and Los Molinos. That river proximity defines the setting: flat agricultural bottomland stretching toward the distant Cascade foothills to the east and Coast Ranges to the west, offering wide-open sky horizons rather than dramatic topography. With a median home value of $265,800 against a median household income of $67,614, the price-to-income ratio lands near 3.9 — genuinely moderate by California standards — while median rent at $877 a month is strikingly low for the state. The tradeoff is stark: this is not a job center but a tiny settlement in a region dominated by agriculture, timber, and public-sector employment, meaning most working residents likely commute to Red Bluff or beyond. At nine hours of daily sunshine and average highs around 77°F, summers run hot in classic Central Valley fashion, while winters stay mild enough for year-round outdoor access along the river corridor. Tehama is essentially a California river hamlet where affordability is real but self-sufficiency is not — nearly everything beyond a front porch requires a drive.
